english.title: Possess extreme pornographic image / images portraying act likely to result in serious injury to person's private parts
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) possessed

(A)_[an extreme pornographic image]_
(B)_[extreme pornographic images, namely **(..SPECIFY NUMBER OF IMAGES..),]_

which portrayed in an explicit and realistic way an act which resulted or was likely to result in serious injury to a person's anus, breasts or genitals and which

(C)_[was]_
(D)_[were]_

grossly offensive, disgusting or otherwise of an obscene character and a reasonable person looking at the image would think that any such person was real
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 63(1), (7)(b) and 67(2) of the Criminal Justice and Immigration Act 2008.

investigatoraction.description: Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

other.penalty:
Summary: Imprisonment for a term not exceeding twelve months and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Three years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit of prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
